title: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”
author: Kallol Bhattacherjee
content_html:
A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India.

“The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG.

The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”.

‘Not unilateral document’

Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama.

The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

title: No power can harm India as long as it reveres Sikh Gurus, says U.P. CM Adityanath
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said that no power in the world will be able to harm India as long as it continues to hold Sikh Gurus in reverence and respect.

“The sacrifice, penance, martyrdom, and spiritual consciousness of the Sikh Gurus are invaluable treasures of India’s national unity, social harmony, and cultural pride,” Mr. Adityanath said, addressing a program organised on the occasion of the 557th Prakash Parv of Sahib Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in Lucknow .

“Through ‘Ek Onkar’, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj gave the message of uniting all humanity. His teachings remain as relevant today as they were then. We must not confine these teachings to events and celebrations alone, but imbibe them in our lives and continuously familiarize the younger generation with them as well,” he added.

Referring to the spiritual and religious significance of Kartik Purnima, the U.P. Chief Minister said, “Today is an extremely sacred day for entire state. Since 4 am, I have been receiving updates on the number of devotees and arrangements at various religious sites across the state. At Shukratal in Muzaffarnagar, lakhs of devotees are taking a holy dip in the Ganga.

At Garhmukteshwar in Hapur, approximately 15 lakh devotees took a holy dip on Tuesday. Meanhwhile, more than 15 lakh devotees took a dip of faith in the Ganga at Tigri in Amroha. A large number of devotees also arrived in Prayagraj and Farrukhabad, while lakhs of them visited the Ganga in Ayodhya and Kashi,”.

Referring to the journeys undertaken by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and social conditions prevailing during his time, Mr. Adityanath said, “When he conveyed the message of unity to humanity, society was grappling with numerous social evils and divisions. Society was fragmented in the name of caste, untouchability and discrimination.

At the same time, he said foreign invasions and external attacks posed challenges. During such difficult times, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj united all humanity through the mantra of ‘Ek Onkar’. His clear message was that God is one and we are all His children. Therefore, every human being deserves equal respect. This mantra, given by him, became a great force for uniting society at that time, and it remains relevant even today. Despite limited means and resources, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj traveled to various places and spread the message of humanity, equality and spiritual consciousness among the masses,”.

Explaining the three principal teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj, ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako’, the U.P. CM added, “Remembering God, performing kirtan and embracing the spirit of togetherness generate positive feelings within human beings. This dispels ignorance and awakens the strength of unity in society,”..

title: Samajwadi Party names five candidates for Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announced five candidates for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls.

The party named Ashu Malik as candidate for the Saharanpur assembly seat, Nahid Hasan for Kairana, Mahboob Ali for Amroha , Jyoti Lodhi for Lalitpur and Umar Ali Khan for the Behat assembly seat.

In a related development, SP president Akhilesh Yadav urged Congress to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for their alliance in most seats, describing the U.P. assembly election as a historic opportunity for secular parties to defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies and save the country from falling into the wrong hands and being ruined.

“This time is a historic opportunity when both of us secular parties can together defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies forever and save the country from falling into wrong hands and getting ruined. We want you and I to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for our “alliance” in most seats. In all the seats we contest, our winning numbers should exceed the number of seats we fail to win. Only victory will make the division respectable, because winning seats brings respect,” he wrote on X.

Mr. Yadav asked Congress to mark all potential seats and send them to the SP.

“We will then discuss together which seat and which candidate is in a position to win. Based on our assessment and mathematical equation for victory, we may also inform the Congress about several winnable seats that they, for some reason, haven’t even considered,” he said.

“Our effort is that when big leaders meet, on all the seats, there should be discussion on the candidate of the ‘INDIA Alliance’ and not the candidate of Congress or the SP, and the thing which will give positive results would be that we present our candidate as the ‘PDA candidate’,” he added.

The SP chief claimed ground surveys have made it clear that the message has reached every city, neighborhood, street, and village that aggrieved and humiliated people from every community and every section of society across the state have rallied against the BJP, believing that the PDA will defeat the NDA and bring about change.

“The truth is, we don’t want seat sharing to be based on a “me-or-you” approach. We don’t want it to be a division, we want to call it ‘seat adjustment’. In seats with difficult equations, we will discuss at least two candidates together, choose the one with the most potential, and work together to ensure their victory. We don’t want alliance candidates to be imposed on each other, but rather, they should be decided by consensus,” he added.

title: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Hardly three days before the retirement of incumbent Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, the Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) proposed the transfer of Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru to the office.

Also read | Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor

The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Sorenwrote to the Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, who is superannuating on November 27.

Mr. Soren had highlighted that a Chief Justice to the State High Court should ideally have been recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium in advance, and cleared by the Union government as per the Memorandum of Procedure for appointment of judges to the constitutional courts.

The Chief Minister, as the head of the State government, had expressed objections about any interim arrangement, making it clear that the State High Court must have a regular Chief Justice at the helm.

Mr. Soren, in his letter to the CJI and the Collegium judges, had reportedly pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment.

On Tuesday (November 24), the Supreme Court Collegium proposed that Justice Bakhru take over as the Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice. The ball is now with the government to clear the Collegium resolution and notify the appointment of Justice Bakhru by November 27.

The Collegium has recommended Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court, to be transferred as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court in the place of Justice Bakhru.

In a separate resolution on November 24, the Collegium recommended the appointment of Himachal Pradesh High Court judge, Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court following the transfer of Justice Rao to the Karnataka High Court.

title: Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained
author: Kartikey  Singh
content_html:
The story so far: On November 22, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the country’s apex food-safety regulator, sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. after a sample of its water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards, with the regulator declaring it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The public-health stakes are significant. In 2023, bottled water was the principal source of drinking water for 15% of urban and 6% of rural households, as per Data For India. For consumers buying it at railway stations, airports, highway eateries and neighbourhood shops, a sealed bottle is often taken as an assurance of safety. Yet, the data submitted in Parliament in February 2025 revealed that 333 of 1,300 enforcement samples of packaged drinking water tested in 2023-24 failed to meet prescribed standards. Similarly, in 2022-23, 650 of 1,776 samples had been found non-compliant.

According to the FSSAI, a sample of packaged drinking water (other than mineral water) collected from Bisleri’s premises was found to be non-compliant with the prescribed limits for “bromate” and was declared unsafe under the 2006 Act. Following an appeal by the food business operator (FBO), the sample was referred to a Referral Food Laboratory for further examination, which also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of “polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons” (PAHs).

In its response, Bisleri has maintained that its water is safe for consumption, saying the matter concerned a batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025, one of 143 manufacturing plants in its network. In a statement issued on November 23, the company said the FSSAI had collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025. While five samples met the prescribed standards, the sixth recorded a “bromate” level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre. Further, Bisleri said it appealed on November 22, 2025, following which the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting. The laboratory, as claimed, found the bromate level within the prescribed limit but separately detected PAHs. Citing the divergent test findings, the company reportedly arranged an independent examination of the same sample at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which, according to Bisleri, also found the bromate level within limits. The company said it submitted these results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office on February 2, 2026, but received no further communication and understood that the matter had been closed.

Water is essential for digestion, blood circulation, temperature regulation and kidney function, but its safety cannot be judged by its appearance, taste, odour or sealed packaging alone. Contamination may be microbiological, causing illnesses such as diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid, or chemical, with some substances posing risks through prolonged exposure. In India, packaged water broadly falls into two categories: (1) “packaged drinking water”, which may be sourced from surface water, groundwater or seawater and treated through processes such as filtration, decantation, reverse osmosis (RO) and disinfection; and (2) “natural mineral water”, drawn from protected underground sources and characterised by a relatively stable mineral composition. Both must meet prescribed chemical and microbiological safety standards.

title: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Saudi capital
author: PTI
content_html:
Two Indians and three Nepalese nationals were among 11 people injured on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) when Yemen's Houthi militia targeted a tower in the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital, authorities said.

Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said 11 people were injured after the tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia.

Those injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indian nationals, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, it said.

It added that competent authorities immediately responded to the incident, implemented all approved procedures and measures for handling such situations, and took the necessary measures to protect lives and property.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also confirmed that two Indian nationals sustained injuries in the attack.

In a post on X, it said further details are being ascertained and all possible assistance will be extended to the injured persons and their families.

Earlier, Saudi-led Coalition Spokesperson Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said a tower had been targeted in the financial district and that competent authorities were responding at the site.

Meanwhile, the Indian embassy also asked Indian nationals residing in the Gulf country to abide by local rules and regulations.

The Houthis have in the past claimed responsibility for attacks on Riyadh.

Two Indians and three Nepalese nationals were among 11 people injured on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) when Yemen's Houthi militia targeted a tower in the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital, authorities said.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said 11 people were injured after the tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia.
Those injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indian nationals, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, it said.
It added that competent authorities immediately responded to the incident, implemented all approved procedures and measures for handling such situations, and took the necessary measures to protect lives and property.
The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also confirmed that two Indian nationals sustained injuries in the attack.
In a post on X, it said further details are being ascertained and all possible assistance will be extended to the injured persons and their families.
Earlier, Saudi-led Coalition Spokesperson Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said a tower had been targeted in the financial district and that competent authorities were responding at the site.
Meanwhile, the Indian embassy also asked Indian nationals residing in the Gulf country to abide by local rules and regulations.
The Houthis have in the past claimed responsibility for attacks on Riyadh.
